# Results — Study 822 (Omega-Ratio Sort)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Keating
& Shadwick (2002): the **Omega ratio** at threshold 0, `Ω(0) = E[max(r,0)] / E[max(−r,0)]`,
is a gain/loss ratio that uses the *whole* return distribution (every moment), so a
long-high-Omega / short-low-Omega sort should **beat a plain trailing-Sharpe sort** (study
814). Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is
dropped). Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close). Sample as-of 2026-06-30.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **trailing 12-1 Omega(0)** = mean positive daily return ÷ mean absolute negative daily return over a 252-day formation window that **ends 21 days ago** (skips the most recent month, à la 12-1 momentum), known at the close of `t−1` (one further `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the signal; **long the top 30%** (high Omega), **short the bottom 30%** (low Omega), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Comparators | plain **trailing Sharpe** (mean ÷ std, study 814) and a pure **low-vol** sort, identical universe/dates/machinery, plus the average per-day rank correlation of the signals |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled high-vs-low books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**.

## The headline — long-high-Omega / short-low-Omega spread

Daily equal-weight top-30% minus bottom-30% trailing-Omega spread (n = **3,873** days,
median 50 names/day):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long high-Omega − short low-Omega)** | **+1.19 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **+0.76** |
| one-sample *t* | +0.72 |
| high-Omega book / low-Omega book | +7.93 bps / +6.74 bps (Welch *t* = +0.42) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | 0.18 |

The claimed edge has the **right sign but is not significant** (NW *t* = +0.76, well below
the |t| ≥ 2 bar): on 50 liquid US mega-caps a long-high-Omega / short-low-Omega book earns a
statistically indistinguishable-from-zero +1.19 bps/day.

## Does the full gain/loss ratio beat Sharpe? — the head-to-head (the whole point)

Same universe, same dates, same sort machinery:

| sort | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| trailing **Omega(0)** (long high / short low) | **+1.19 bps** | +0.76 |
| trailing **Sharpe** (long high / short low) | +1.29 bps | +0.83 |
| pure **low-vol** (long low-vol / short high-vol) | −5.65 bps | −2.92 |

| overlap | value |
|---|--:|
| avg per-day rank corr **Omega ~ Sharpe** | **+0.996** |
| avg per-day rank corr **Omega ~ (−vol)** | +0.075 |

The answer to the honesty question is unambiguous: the Omega sort is **99.6% rank-correlated
with the Sharpe sort** — it re-picks almost exactly the names Sharpe already picks — and it
does **not** beat it (Omega +1.19 bps vs Sharpe +1.29 bps; if anything a hair *worse*). The
"full distribution" the Omega ratio is sold on buys nothing here: on daily equity returns
`Ω(0)` is a near-monotone re-labelling of mean-over-vol, and it inherits Sharpe's
insignificance rather than curing it. (The low-vol confound is *not* the driver — Omega ~
(−vol) is only +0.075; Omega tracks Sharpe, and Sharpe here is essentially momentum.)

## Placebo — is the spread a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the trailing-Omega sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted**
panel (signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **+1.19 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.087 bps (0.980) |
| right-tail p | **0.120** |

The observed +1.19 bps sits ≈1.1σ above a null centred at zero — inside the noise (p = 0.12),
consistent with the insignificant NW *t*.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,739) | +0.29 bps | +0.16 |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | +1.92 bps | +0.80 |

Neither half clears the bar; the (weak, positive) tilt is a little stronger post-2018 but
never significant.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +1.19 bps | 2.14 bps | **−0.95 bps** | −0.58 | −0.15 | −2.4%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +1.19 bps | 10.14 bps | **−8.95 bps** | −5.44 | −1.39 | −22.6%/yr |

The +1.19 bps/day gross edge is already thinner than the 2.14 bps/day round-trip friction at a
mere 1 bp one-way, so the book is **net-negative at every realistic cost**. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent latent "quality tilt" that sets each name's
volatility (high tilt → low vol → high Omega against a steady drift) and, with `edge>0`, lifts
its forward mean. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.05** (sd 1.00), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.0016`, seed 822) | **+9.67** (Welch *t* = +9.49) |

The detector recovers a *planted* high-Omega → high-return relation cleanly and stays quiet on
the null (1/20 ≈ the nominal 5% false-positive rate) — so the flat real-tape result is a true
null, not a broken sort. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The Omega ratio's "whole-distribution" advantage does **not** materialise
  on 50 liquid US mega-caps. The specified long-high-Omega / short-low-Omega spread is
  **+1.19 bps/day** (NW *t* = **+0.76**) — right sign, but nowhere near the |t| ≥ 2 bar,
  insignificant in both eras (*t* = +0.16 / +0.80) and inside a 1,000-permutation placebo
  (p = 0.12). Crucially it is **99.6% rank-identical to a plain trailing-Sharpe sort** and does
  **not beat it** (Sharpe +1.29 bps) — so the extra moments Omega sees add nothing over
  mean/vol. A clean 20-seed synthetic control confirms the machinery would fire on a real
  effect. Survivorship biases the magnitude upward, if anything.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The book is net-negative at every realistic cost (−0.95 bps/day at
  1 bp one-way, −8.95 at 5 bps); the thin gross edge is eaten whole by the round-trip friction.
